newsitem.title: USA: IBM expands licensing of Sun's Java.
newsitem.headline: IBM expands licensing of Sun's Java.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp, in a further endorsement of Sun Microsystems Inc's Java platform, said it was licensing the JavaOS operating system and its HotJava object technology.
IBM said it also was establishing two Java Validation Centers for programmers seeking to ensure their Java software runs effectively on IBM and other hardware platforms.
"We are joined at the hip with JavaSoft (Sun's subsidiary for Java)," David Gee, IBM's head of worldwide Java marketing, said in a conference call.
"Our goal is to exponentially increase the number of lines of Java running worldwide."

In a third part of the agreement, IBM will be able to re- license Java technologies to others, and said it expects its microelectronics group would have further announcements about its intentions in this area in the near future.
Jon Kannegaard, vice president of software at Sun's JavaSoft unit, which was established early this year to foster the growth of the technology, plans to develop a further Java branding program soon.
IBM said it was establishing its Java validation centers initially in San Mateo, Calif., and Waltham, Mass., and it was locating a Java Project office near JavaSoft.
"When you want a Java seal of approval, IBM is going to be the place where you can come and get it," Gee said. "Our intention is to take that worldwide."

"IBM is funding the Java validation centers, and our objective is to allow third party developers to write applications and make sure that they run effectively on our equipment and the equipment of others," the executive said.

JavaOS is a lightweight operating platform for use on network computers, which are designed to offer low-cost computing capabilities. IBM said it intends to offer JavaOS as an option on future network computers it sells.

HotJava is a set of building blocks that can be used to make software applications that function well across networks. For example, Sun has created a HotJava browser which can be used as a graphical interface for network computers.

IBM plans to have the capability to run the Java Virtual Machine technology shipping or in beta testing on all of its machines, including AS/400 midrange computers and its S/390 mainframe family, by the end of this year.
